text.arabic_uthmani: ذَٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتُوا۟ بِٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهَآ أَوْ يَخَافُوٓا۟ أَن تُرَدَّ أَيْمَٰنٌۢ بَعْدَ أَيْمَٰنِهِمْ ۗ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱسْمَعُوا۟ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative pointing back to the counter-oath procedure
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) does not point to a nearby noun; it compresses the counter-oath procedure of 5:107 into a single referent so 5:108 can judge that procedure. The distance of the demonstrative makes the legal mechanism available as a whole, not as a fresh description.

topics.headline: demonstrative compresses the prior procedure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole prior counter-oath mechanism gathered into one evaluative pointer instead of being retold.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows converge on an anaphoric, fronted demonstrative that launches the rationale clause by gathering the previous procedure.

words.gloss_range: elative predicate meaning nearer, lower, or more fitting, locally used for procedural approximation
words.root_gloss_range: root range of nearness, lowness, and approach; local force is legal fitness rather than mere spatial closeness
words.prose: {{ar:أَدْنَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:adnā}}) is an elative predicate: the procedure is closer, more fitting, or at the needed threshold for the two outcomes that follow, not a guarantee that the outcomes will occur. Its range is narrowed by the legal frame, while the same procedural formula is visible in marriage and debt documentation as well (4:3; 2:282; 5:108).

topics.headline: elative nearness becomes legal threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the procedure is evaluated as the nearest workable path to truthful testimony and exposure, not as an absolute guarantee.
topics.reason: The rows preserve nearness and lower-threshold imagery, but QAC and attachment evidence make the local predicate a legal-evaluative judgment.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive particle introducing the first result or purpose clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) binds the elative judgment to the first verbal outcome: that the witnesses produce the testimony. The short particle turns the assessment into a purpose/result clause.

topics.headline: first purpose particle opens desired outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the evaluation immediately tied to a concrete desired outcome rather than left abstract.
topics.reason: Grammar and form rows agree that the first particle governs the subjunctive verb and supplies the first desired outcome.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive Form I plural verb governed by the first purpose particle; with the following preposition it means bring or produce
words.root_gloss_range: root range of coming, arriving, bringing, and performing; the following preposition selects productive bringing here

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition that narrows the verb into bringing with carried content

words.prose: {{ar:يَأْتُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) keeps the witnesses as performers, but the following {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) narrows coming into bringing or producing. The verb therefore governs both the testimony and its proper manner: contested claims are meant to become deliverable evidence.

topics.headline: coming becomes producing testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the legal aim is not mere arrival by witnesses but the production of testimony as evidence.
topics.reason: The rows about subjunctive dependency, productive bringing, Form I performance, and the governed phrases are coherent once the prepositional construction narrows the root.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the carried content or means of the act
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) visibly attaches the verb to the testimony, making the testimony the means or content brought forward. This small preposition keeps the clause evidentiary rather than merely spatial.

topics.headline: preposition binds bringing to testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the verb cannot be read as simple arrival: the testimony is the carried content of the action.
topics.reason: The particle rows all point to the same local function: binding the verb to the testimony complement.

words.gloss_range: definite masdar/gerund for the specific testimony required in the legal case
words.root_gloss_range: root range of witnessing, presence, testimony, and martyrdom; local sense is legal testimony rooted in witnessed presence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the testimony as brought content

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ}} ({{tr:al-shahādati}}) is the definite act of testimony governed by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}). The witnessing root keeps the pressure of present, accountable truth-declaration, while the legal passage spans deathbed testimony, counter-oath, and rationale (5:106; 5:107; 5:108).

topics.headline: definite testimony names the required act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the aim is the specific act of truthful testimony, not a generic witness or a private claim.
topics.reason: The rows about governance, definiteness, masdar form, and the three-ayah testimony unit survive; broader martyrdom associations are background, not the selected local sense.

words.gloss_range: preposition introducing the manner or standard phrase
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) introduces the standard under which the testimony is delivered. Its spatial overness is narrowed into conformity: the testimony is to come upon its proper face.

topics.headline: overness becomes conformity to proper form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that testimony must be brought according to its proper standard, not simply brought.
topics.reason: Attachment and grammar rows support manner or conformity here; possible attachment to either the act of bringing or the testimony does not change the local payoff.

words.gloss_range: genitive noun with feminine suffix referring back to the testimony, meaning its face, aspect, or proper manner
words.root_gloss_range: root range of face, direction, aspect, orientation, and manner; local sense is the testimony’s proper form while the face image remains active

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the testimony whose suffix supplies the referent

words.prose: {{ar:وَجْهِهَآ}} ({{tr:wajhihā}}) gives the testimony its own face: a proper form or aspect that can be preserved or distorted. The suffix points back to {{ar:ٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ}} ({{tr:al-shahādati}}), and the legal use of face-language is distinct from divine countenance passages while still showing a wider range (2:115; 2:272; 5:6).

topics.headline: testimony has its own proper face
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the testimony is treated as having its own objective face, displacing witness-owned versions of the story.
topics.reason: The rows about manner, metaphorical face, singularity, suffix reference, and cross-register face-language are kept, narrowed by the local testimony referent.

words.gloss_range: disjunctive conjunction coordinating two purpose outcomes
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْ}} ({{tr:aw}}) coordinates two outcomes under the same evaluation. First comes the ideal production of testimony; then comes the fallback pressure that they fear oath reversal.

topics.headline: disjunction separates ideal and deterrent outcomes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees two sufficient routes for the procedure: truthful testimony if possible, deterrent fear if not.
topics.reason: The rows agree on coordination of two purpose clauses, with the ordered pairing preserving a hierarchy without collapsing the clauses.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive plural verb parallel to the testimony verb, taking a content clause of feared reversal
words.root_gloss_range: root range of fear, dread, caution, and reverent apprehension; local sense is deterrent fear of oath reversal

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: parallel first dependent outcome in the legal pairing

words.prose: {{ar:يَخَافُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:yakhāfū}}) parallels {{ar:يَأْتُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) as the second dependent outcome. The fear field is narrowed here to deterrent apprehension that their oaths may be answered and reversed, while a comparison with communal duty fear remains only a contextual contrast (5:23; 5:108).

topics.headline: fear becomes legal deterrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the procedure works even through anticipated exposure: fear itself becomes a tool for truthful conduct.
topics.reason: The rows about subjunctive parallelism, feared content, productive fear, and duty-pressure comparison survive when the local object of fear is the reversal clause.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive particle introducing the content of what is feared
words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) opens the content of the fear: that oaths may be returned after their oaths. Its repetition after the first {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) gives the legal logic two audible result clauses, and the comparison with 5:23 marks a different fear-object in 5:108.

topics.headline: second purpose particle opens feared content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the deterrent branch deepen from fear in general to the specific feared event of oath reversal.
topics.reason: The rows cluster around nested clause structure, repeated result framing, and the contrast between fear of God in 5:23 and fear of oath reversal here.

words.gloss_range: passive imperfect/subjunctive verb agreeing with the oath subject, meaning be returned or reversed
words.root_gloss_range: root range of returning, rejecting, repelling, and reversing; local sense is legal reversal of oaths
words.prose: {{ar:تُرَدَّ}} ({{tr:turadda}}) is passive and prospective: oaths may be returned, reversed, or sent back within the legal mechanism. The passive suppresses the human reverser, so fear falls on the procedure itself, with a wider reversal-after-establishment pattern visible by comparison (6:71; 5:108).

topics.headline: passive reversal makes procedure impersonal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the feared event is not a named accuser’s action but an impersonal procedure that can send oaths back against them.
topics.reason: Passive voice, feminine agreement with the broken plural, reversal semantics, and the mirrored oath frame all point to impersonal legal reversal.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative plural oath noun serving as passive subject
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes oath and right-hand imagery; local sense is oaths, with embodied pledge imagery as background

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: passive reversal verb that governs these oaths as subject

words.prose: {{ar:أَيْمَٰنٌۢ}} ({{tr:aymānun}}) is indefinite and nominative as the passive subject of {{ar:تُرَدَّ}} ({{tr:turadda}}). The right-hand imagery remains a background pledge image, but the local meaning is oaths: unspecified counter-oaths that can answer earlier oaths.

topics.headline: indefinite counter-oaths widen the threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that any counter-oaths may rise as the grammatical subject of reversal, not only a named replacement oath.
topics.reason: The grammar rows fix passive-subject status and indefiniteness; the oath/right-hand rows are retained as narrowed embodied background.

words.gloss_range: temporal adverb setting the later position of counter-oaths
words.root_gloss_range: root range of distance, after-ness, and later sequence; local force is temporal succession
words.prose: {{ar:بَعْدَ}} ({{tr:baʿda}}) sets the temporal frame: the counter-oaths come after the first oaths. That after-sequence creates the exposure window, with nearby legal aftermath language also visible in the passage (5:106; 5:108).

topics.headline: afterness creates the exposure window
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the legal pressure depends on sequence: later oaths can expose and undo earlier ones.
topics.reason: The rows consistently make the word a temporal adverbial that enables later correction after initial oath establishment.

words.gloss_range: possessed genitive plural oath noun governed by the temporal adverb
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes oath and right-hand pledge imagery; local sense is their earlier oaths

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: indefinite counter-oaths contrasted with the possessed earlier oaths

words.prose: {{ar:أَيْمَٰنِهِمْ}} ({{tr:aymānihim}}) names their earlier oaths as definite and possessed. Its repetition against {{ar:أَيْمَٰنٌۢ}} ({{tr:aymānun}}) makes a mirror clause: oath after oath, but with indefiniteness on the later counter-oaths and ownership on the first ones.

topics.headline: possessed original oaths contrast with indefinite counter-oaths
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the legal asymmetry: unspecified later oaths are set after the possessed oaths of the original witnesses.
topics.reason: The rows about genitive possession, suffix definiteness, oath repetition, and the 5:89 comparison are preserved as a local contrast in oath liability (5:89; 5:108).

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the imperative unit
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens a new imperative unit after the procedural rationale. The connector keeps continuity, but it also shifts from described legal mechanics into direct communal address.

topics.headline: resumptive connector shifts from procedure to command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the discourse turn from explaining the procedure to directly addressing the community.
topics.reason: The rows identify this connector as resumptive rather than simple coordination, matching the clause boundary before the imperative.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII plural imperative meaning guard yourselves, be mindful, or practice taqwā
words.root_gloss_range: root range of guarding, shielding, and protection; Form VIII makes the guarding reflexive and internalized

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: direct object before whom the guarding command is oriented

words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّقُوا۟}} ({{tr:ittaqū}}) changes explanation into command. Its protective root makes taqwā a reflexive guarding posture before {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}), and the command belongs to a recurring Surah 5 legal refrain (5:2; 5:4; 5:7; 5:8; 5:11; 5:35; 5:57; 5:88; 5:96; 5:100; 5:108).

topics.headline: guarding command internalizes the legal procedure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witness procedure ends by turning courtroom mechanics into a guarded moral posture before God.
topics.reason: The rows about imperative force, Form VIII reflexivity, protective imagery, cadence, and Surah 5 recurrence survive with the local object supplied by the next word.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as accusative object of the guarding command
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name root field can be discussed derivationally, but the local word is the proper name and object of command

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: command verb that takes the divine name as object

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) is the accusative object of {{ar:ٱتَّقُوا۟}} ({{tr:ittaqū}}). The divine-name derivation remains background; the local payoff is role and authority, especially because the name returns as nominative subject in the final maxim, with an oath-law comparison also in view (5:89; 5:108).

topics.headline: divine name is object of guarded awareness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the case-role movement: God is first the object before whom the community must guard itself, then the subject of the closing verdict.
topics.reason: The rows about accusative object status, divine authority, case alternation, and the 5:89 comparison are retained while avoiding overreading derivational speculation as the local sense.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction linking the second imperative to the first
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second imperative with the first, making guarded awareness and listening a command-pair. The same paired-command closure links different legal domains in Surah 5 (5:2; 5:108), while the local sequence of connectors marks command opening, command pairing, and final declaration.

topics.headline: connector pairs guarding with listening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the two commands as one response posture: guarded awareness joined to receptive obedience.
topics.reason: The rows support coordination of imperatives, a recurring closing command comparison, and the local three-connector discourse progression (5:106; 5:107; 5:108; 5:51).

words.gloss_range: objectless plural imperative meaning listen, hear, or receive obediently
words.root_gloss_range: root range of hearing, listening, and receptive obedience; local command is open-ended because no object is stated
words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْمَعُوا۟}} ({{tr:ismaʿū}}) is an objectless imperative, so the hearing remains open-ended. It turns the audience from observers of witness procedure into receivers of the command; the contrast with a failed hearing response sharpens the demand (2:93; 5:108).

topics.headline: objectless listening widens obedience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is not limited to one quoted instruction; the community is summoned into receptive obedience to the whole legal warning.
topics.reason: The rows about no explicit object, command force, hearing-as-obedience, shared imperative cadence, and the 2:93 comparison survive; the local syntax blocks supplying a specific object.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction before the final nominal/declarative clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the closing declaration. It is not a third imperative; it attaches the command-pair to a final divine principle about guidance and boundary-rupture.

topics.headline: resumptive connector opens the final maxim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the final sentence as attached to the commands yet lifted into a general principle.
topics.reason: The rows agree that the connector is resumptive before the final declarative closure, preserving both linkage and clause shift.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as nominative subject of the negated guidance clause
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name root field is background; local role is the nominative proper-name subject of the guidance verdict
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) repeats the divine name instead of using a pronoun, and its nominative role makes God the subject of the closing verdict. The repeated name tracks the shift from object of communal taqwā to subject of divine non-guidance.

topics.headline: divine name becomes subject of the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from human responsibility to divine agency: God is now the subject who withholds guidance.
topics.reason: The rows about explicit repetition, nominative case, divine agency, and the tadhyīl-style closure all support the same role-shift payoff.

words.gloss_range: negative particle scoping over the imperfect guidance verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) negates the imperfect guidance verb and gives the ending a categorical force. The legal procedure closes with a standing denial of guidance for the class named at the end.

topics.headline: negation turns guidance into a standing denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closure as a standing rule, not a one-time refusal in a single court case.
topics.reason: All rows point to negation over the imperfect verb and to the generalizing force of the final maxim.

words.gloss_range: transitive imperfect guidance verb under negation, taking the collective as object
words.root_gloss_range: root range of guiding, leading, path-indication, and gift/offering; local sense is divine guidance withheld, with gift-like generosity as a secondary pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يَهْدِى}} ({{tr:yahdī}}) is transitive here: the object is the people named next. The path-guidance sense is primary, while the gift branch adds the sense of withheld divine generosity; the wider non-guidance collective formula varies its final qualifier across passages (5:51; 62:5; 5:67; 2:264; 5:108; 9:24; 61:5; 63:6).

topics.headline: guidance is withheld from a defined collective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witness-law warning ends as a guidance relation: a defined collective loses divine direction and generosity because of fisq.
topics.reason: The rows about imperfect negation, transitivity, path-indication, gift pressure, co-occurrence, formula recurrence, and Surah 5 closure are retained with local grammar selecting transitive guidance.

words.gloss_range: definite collective noun as direct object of the guidance verb
words.root_gloss_range: root range of standing, rising, maintaining, station, and collective people; local sense is a definite people while standing imagery colors the group identity
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقَوْمَ}} ({{tr:al-qawma}}) is the direct object of the negated guidance verb. The collective noun makes fisq a group identity, and the standing-root handoff from procedural replacement to communal verdict links the prior mechanism to this final class (5:107; 5:108).

topics.headline: the people are a defined collective object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that non-guidance falls on a standing collective, not merely scattered individual offenders.
topics.reason: The rows about accusative object status, collective force, definiteness with the following qualifier, and the q-w-m handoff survive, narrowed to the local noun meaning people.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural active participle qualifying the collective object
words.root_gloss_range: root range of exiting, splitting out, and boundary rupture; local sense is the known class characterized by fisq in the testimony context

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: collective noun qualified by the final participle

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ}} ({{tr:al-fāsiqīn}}) is the ayah's final word, agreeing with {{ar:ٱلْقَوْمَ}} ({{tr:al-qawma}}) and landing the verdict on the moral cause for non-guidance. The active participle makes the label persistent, the rupture image fits oath-breaking in this testimony context, and the phrase links the legal closure with the same Surah 5 collective verdict (5:25; 5:26; 5:108).

topics.headline: final participle lands on ongoing boundary rupture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah’s last word names an ongoing collective condition: people who rupture the oath-boundary are the class God does not guide.
topics.reason: The rows about adjective agreement, final-word landing, active-participle persistence, rupture imagery, Surah 5 recurrence, cadence, and movement from wrongdoing to collective fisq are retained, with the root image narrowed to the local oath-boundary setting.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction 'bring the testimony on its face' at 5:108 words 4-7.
baseline_models.mechanism: Arrival, knowledgeable declaration, and the right face or direction combine into a delivery rule: evidence must enter the procedure in a form whose presentation is aligned with its matter.

activation_trace.role: Coming and arrival supply the act of bringing evidence into the procedure.
Knowledge-based declaration supplies the evidentiary content that must be delivered.
The sound face of an affair supplies correctness of form, direction, and handling.

changed_reading.before: The witnesses are simply told to state the truth.
changed_reading.after: The verse seeks testimony that is brought into view through its proper procedural face, joining truthful content to correct presentation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The alternative 'or they fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths' at 5:108 words 8-14.
baseline_models.mechanism: Expected harm is attached to a repeatable oath sequence: an oath can fail acceptance or be met by a later oath, so the first speakers do not control the final evidentiary record.

activation_trace.role: Fear as expectation of a signaled harm supplies the deterrent force.
Rejection of a false or defective item makes nonacceptance of the first oaths a live consequence.
Repetition and return supply the second evidentiary turn rather than a final first oath.
The oath and sworn undertaking supply both layers of binding speech.
Later succession after an earlier act orders the two oath layers in time.

changed_reading.before: The witnesses are deterred by a general fear of punishment.
changed_reading.after: They are deterred by a specific loss of oath finality: a later sworn layer can reject, answer, or displace their own.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The closing sequence 'be wary of God and hear; God does not guide the transgressing people' at 5:108 words 15-22.
baseline_models.mechanism: Self-protection is completed by receptive compliance, while guidance is the route that remains available to a responsive community; the close therefore makes the procedure an ethical practice, not merely a spoken warning.

activation_trace.role: Placing oneself in protection supplies deliberate restraint against the feared breach.
Hearing as understanding and compliance turns reception of the rule into action.
Gentle direction to a path or truth supplies the route forfeited by persistent noncompliance.
A human group supplies the communal scale on which hearing or refusal operates.

changed_reading.before: The ending adds generic piety and an instruction to listen.
changed_reading.after: The ending requires protective restraint and operative compliance, locating evidentiary integrity in the practice of a whole community.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier oath regulation separates speech that is discarded from oaths that are deliberately bound, repaired, and preserved; this gives the two oath layers in 5:108 legal custody and consequence.

activation_trace.role: The two focus occurrences supply the sequence of sworn undertakings being regulated.
Discarded, uncounted speech supplies the negative category against which accountable oaths are distinguished.
Repeated oath language supplies a regulated class of binding speech rather than an isolated utterance.
Binding and ratifying an undertaking supplies the point at which an oath becomes accountable.
Persistent guarding supplies continuing custody of what was sworn.

structural_cues: 5:89 contrasts idle oath with contracted oath, assigns expiation, and commands preservation of oaths.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies distinct oath classes, binding, repair, and preservation; I infer that the later-after-earlier oaths in 5:108 operate inside that accountable oath economy. A live alternative is that 5:89 regulates personal vows while 5:108 uses oath only as courtroom speech.

changed_reading.before: The repeated oaths in 5:108 are momentary assertions within one dispute.
changed_reading.after: They are accountable undertakings with custody: binding speech can be tested, repaired, superseded, and still remains chargeable to its speakers.

context_deltas.mechanism: The polarity between making something appear and concealing it turns the testimony's proper face into an inspectability condition: its matter must be exposed rather than held behind an acceptable exterior.

activation_trace.role: The sound face of an affair supplies the focus requirement of proper handling.
The outwardly declaring tongue supplies testimony's capacity to expose its speaker's account.
Emergence into visibility supplies the positive pole of inspectable evidence.
Hiding and covering supply the failure that a merely presentable face could mask.

structural_cues: 5:99 places what people make manifest and what they conceal in a direct pair under divine knowledge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies manifestation versus concealment; I infer that 'on its face' demands an account open to inspection, not only formal correctness. The live alternative is that the phrase means correctness without adding a disclosure criterion.

changed_reading.before: The testimony's proper face is chiefly its correct form or direction.
changed_reading.after: Its proper face is also anti-concealment: the evidentiary matter must become inspectable rather than merely wear a correct exterior.

context_deltas.mechanism: Doubt initiates sworn examination; discovery of concealed fault activates another pair, who stand in the first pair's place and submit a competing truth claim. The feared 'return' in 5:108 is therefore a concrete review and substitution loop.

activation_trace.role: Rejection of a defective claim supplies the focus consequence imposed on the first oaths.
The before-and-after sworn undertakings supply the two evidentiary turns.
A formally apportioned oath supplies the first pair's sworn procedural act.
Disturbing doubt supplies the condition that activates examination rather than automatic acceptance.
Coming upon something hidden supplies the discovery event that reopens the record.
Competing parties each asserting the right supplies the adversarial comparison of the two testimonies.

identity_judgment.rationale: Hazırlanan dal, kaynak ifadesindeki ortak çekirdeği doğru biçimde karşılar: bilinen ya da sanılan bir belirtiye dayanarak istenmeyen bir şey beklemek kişide korku ve ürküntü doğurur. Kaynakların korkuyu güven içinde olmanın karşıtı sayması da aynı sınır içinde kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın korku çekirdeği ile belirli söz öbeklerine ve katılımcı ilişkilerine bağlı kullanımlar ayrı tutulur; çok korkan kişi veya topluluk anlatımları ve başkası için korkma kullanımı yalın anlamın tamamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bilinen ya da sanılan bir belirtiye dayanarak istenmeyen bir şeyin gerçekleşmesini beklerken duyulan korku ve ürküntü halidir; güven içinde olmanın karşıtıdır.

facets.statement: İstenmeyen bir olayın gerçekleşeceği, bilinen ya da sanılan bir belirtiye dayanılarak beklenir.
Bu beklenti kişide korku, ürküntü ve kaçınma eğilimi doğuran bir ruh hali olarak yaşanır.
Kavram, kişinin kendisini güven içinde hissettiği durumun karşı kutbunu oluşturur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar korku ve ürküntüyü ortak çekirdek olarak verir. Bazı anlatımlar bu hali güvenin karşıtı diye sınırlar, bazıları ise bilinen ya da sanılan bir belirtiden hareketle kötü bir sonuç bekleme yönünü açıklar. Kaynaklar, çoğul biçimin bu kök altında değerlendirilip değerlendirilmemesi konusunda ayrılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kötü sonuç beklentisini, belirtiye dayanmayı ve bunun doğurduğu korku halini birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Toplu kaynak ifadesi hem bir şeyin ya da kişinin önceki yerine veya durumuna dönmesini hem de onun oraya döndürülmesini açıkça ortak çekirdek olarak verir. Görmenin yeniden kazanılması bu çekirdeğin bir durumun geri gelmesi biçimindeki özel gerçekleşmesidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dönüş çekirdeğini korur; yön bildiren, yetki devreden ve belirli bir durumun geri gelmesini anlatan yapılar ayrı özel kullanımlar olarak tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin veya kişinin önceki yerine, sahibine ya da durumuna dönmesi yahut bir etken tarafından oraya döndürülmesidir. Kaybolmuş bir işlevin yeniden kazanılması da aynı geri gelme düzeninin özel bir görünümüdür.

facets.statement: Hareketin temel yönü, bir varlığın daha önce bulunduğu yere veya duruma geri gelmesidir.
Geçişli kullanımda bir etken, şeyi yerine, sahibine veya bağlı olduğu merciye geri gönderir.
Bir yetinin yeniden ortaya çıkması, önceki durumun geri kazanılması olarak kavranır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortaklaştırılmış anlatımı, kendiliğinden geri gelme ile bir şeyi geri gönderme biçimlerini tek dönüş çekirdeğinde birleştirir; yer, sahip, merci ve önceki işlev bu yönün farklı hedefleridir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir varlığın önceki yerine, sahibine ya da durumuna yöneldiği hem geçişsiz hem geçişli kullanımlar için uygundur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Toplu kaynak ifadesi kabul etmeme, sözü yanlış sayma ve sahte olduğu anlaşılan parayı geri çevirme kullanımlarını açıkça bir araya getirir. Dal çerçevesi, geri göndermeyi tek başına değil olumsuz değerlendirme sonucuna bağlı olarak sunar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam, bir şeyi kişiye karşı geri çeviren veya sahte parayı geri veren yapılara bağlıdır; yalın kök için genel reddetme anlamı kurulmaz.

concept_map.definition: Sunulan bir şeyi kabul etmeyip sahibine geri çevirmek veya bir söz ya da iddiayı yanlış ve geçersiz saymaktır. Daha önce alınmış sahte paranın denetleyene geri verilmesi bu değerlendirmenin somut ticari örneğidir.

facets.statement: Nesne, söz veya iddia olumsuz değerlendirme sonucunda kabul edilmez.
Bir sözü yanlış saymak, kabul etmemenin doğruluk değerlendirmesine uygulanmış biçimidir.
Sahte olduğu belirlenen paranın onu denetleyene geri verilmesi, kabul etmemenin ticari örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortaklaştırılmış ifade, reddetme eylemini kabul ve doğruluk değerlendirmesine bağlar; sahte paranın geri çevrilmesi bu çekirdeğin nesnel bir denetim sonucunda gerçekleşen örneğidir.

Elin ağza götürüldüğü ifade yalnızca sözlüksel birimdir ve çoklu yorumları dal çekirdeğine dönüştürülmemelidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yineleme, gidip gelme, kararsızlık ve sıkı yapılı kişi anlamları ayrılır; el-ağız ifadesinin tartışmalı yorumları yalın anlama katılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi yeniden yeniden yapmak veya bir varlığın iki yön arasında gidip gelmesidir; karar verememe bu hareket düzeninin zihinsel uzantısıdır. Parçaları birbirine bindirilmiş gibi sıkı ve toplu yapılı insan da benzetme yoluyla böyle adlandırılır.

facets.statement: Bir eylem veya hareket bir defadan sonra yeniden gerçekleşir.
Aynı iki yön veya yer arasında tekrar tekrar gidip gelme, hareketin belirli biçimidir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal kabuğun yapısını ve çok katlı oluşunu adlandırır; odak dal ise belirli bir meyvenin kabuğundan çıkma olayını anlatır. Ortak katılımcı, ortak anlam çekirdeği oluşturmaz.

root_profile.summary: Kökün anlam örgüsü, bağlı bulunulan bir sınırın dışına çıkma tasarımı çevresinde itaat ve buyruktan kopmayı, taze hurmanın kabuğundan çıkışını ve fare için kullanılan küçültmeli kötüleme adını bir araya getirir. Son iki dal, ilk dalın davranışsal anlamını doğrudan paylaşmaz; somut çıkış ve bu çıkışla ya da kötücül sayılmayla açıklanan adlandırma yönünde ayrı uzantılardır.
